get.description:
Public school feed; optional ``start_utc``/``end_utc`` window.

``start_utc`` keeps occurrences still on at it: ending at or after it, or with
no end, starting no more than the no-end visibility window before it.
``include_past`` drops the default start-of-today lower bound, so a caller
can ask for a host's full history. Omits ``created_by``.

post.description:
Record a batch of event interactions and position clicks.

Auth via ``Authorization: Bearer`` (frontend uses ``fetch`` + ``keepalive``
so the header works on unload). Authenticated batches are size-capped and
deduped; payload ``user_id`` must match the authenticated user.
Anonymous requests are allowed for basic click tracking and are
IP-rate-limited; without ``user_id`` they cannot drive personalized signals.

competition.title: Competition
competition.description: An event where participants compete for rankings, judging, prizes or a winner, including hackathons, case competitions, contests and tournaments. Classify this individual event, not other events mentioned in a shared caption. Practice sessions, ordinary workshops, application announcements, raffles, ticket giveaways, watch parties and award ceremonies without competitive presentations do not qualify. Use null when competition is unconfirmed.

employers_on_campus.title: Employers On Campus
employers_on_campus.description: Networking opportunities: true when meeting people who can help students' careers is part of this event. That covers employers, companies, firms or industry organizations recruiting, presenting, hosting, co-hosting or sponsoring it (a company named as host or co-host, such as "Ramp x Blueprint" or "Figma x Sanrio", qualifies even for a social); career fairs, employer information sessions and co-op or internship sessions; professionals or alumni sharing their careers or networking with students; career-path panels and advice sessions on breaking into an industry, including ones led by upper-year students; hackathons, designathons, datathons, case competitions and pitch competitions; and professional, industry or academic conferences, symposiums and summits. Online events and events off campus qualify. Ordinary club socials, meetings and workshops with no company, professional or career element, language and gift exchanges, study-abroad, exchange-program and grad school information, wellness, cultural, religious and community-service events, food distributions and performances do not qualify. Require event-specific evidence in the caption or poster; a post with no event details, such as a link-in-bio or weekly roundup post, establishes nothing. Classify this individual event, not other events in a shared caption. Use false when the event clearly has no networking element and null when that is uncertain.

sports_game.title: Sports Game
sports_game.description: An actual scheduled athletic game, match, meet, or tournament involving an official school varsity team. Intramural, club-team, and recreational competitions, practices, tryouts, fitness classes, sports-club meetings, video games, and watch parties do not qualify. School affiliation or posting from an athletics account alone does not establish varsity participation. Use null when official varsity participation is unconfirmed.

Null means unreviewed or uncertain; an empty array means reviewed with no matching season. Display windows control filter visibility, not classification. Event dates alone do not prove thematic membership.

EventResponse.title: EventResponse
EventResponse.description:
Full event payload returned from GET /events/{id} and used internally
for ownership checks.

``created_by`` is retained here because the field is load-bearing for
the authorization layer (``get_authorized_resource`` reads it); the
public list endpoint hides it via ``EventSummaryResponse`` which
omits the field entirely.

``occurrences`` is the canonical date list.

EventSummaryResponse.title: EventSummaryResponse
EventSummaryResponse.description:
Payload for list/card views.

Description is included because the feed search matches event copy as well
as titles, hosts, locations, and food.

The owning club's display/link/social fields (``club_logo_url``,
``club_type``, ``club_page``, ``club_ig``,
``club_discord``) are
embedded read-time from the ``clubs`` row via the
``events.club_id`` FK so the event card can render without a second
fetch.

``created_by`` is intentionally omitted - this response is returned on
public GET /events/ and would otherwise leak the creator's user ID
to anonymous callers.

InteractionBatch.title: InteractionBatch
InteractionBatch.description:
Batch of interactions submitted from a single browser session.

**Trust boundary note on ``user_id``**: this field models the client's
*claim* of which user the batch belongs to.  The server verifies the
claim against the authenticated identity in ``interaction_service._validate_batch``
and 403s on mismatch.  The field is **advisory / diagnostic** -
never trust it for authorization or identity resolution in new code;
use the value resolved from the Bearer token instead.

Typed as ``UUID | None`` so the Pydantic boundary rejects arbitrary
opaque strings (e.g. ``"admin"``) at parse time - if the router-side
ownership check is ever removed during a refactor, impersonation
still cannot succeed because the payload won't even deserialise.
